task_description: Renal toxicity prediction - predict whether a drug causes toxic damage to the kidneys (e.g., acute kidney injury, reduced renal function, nephropathy). Renal handling of drugs is common, but nephrotoxicity is class-specific: most drugs are eliminated by the kidney without injuring it, and toxicity is confined to agents that reach cytotoxic concentrations in tubular cells, precipitate in the lumen, or measurably disrupt glomerular hemodynamics or the filtration barrier.
prediction_question: Does this molecule exhibit renal toxicity? Your final answer should be formatted as either: 'Final answer: Toxicity' or 'Final answer: Non-toxicity'.

OAT1.logic: OAT1 (SLC22A6) is a basolateral organic anion transporter of proximal tubule cells. It couples uptake to an outwardly directed dicarboxylate gradient, drawing anionic substrates such as antiviral nucleotide analogs, NSAIDs, methotrexate, and beta-lactams from blood into the tubular epithelium.
OAT1.logic_cited: OAT1 (SLC22A6) is a basolateral organic anion transporter of proximal tubule cells[3][4t]. It couples uptake to an outwardly directed dicarboxylate gradient[4t], drawing anionic substrates such as antiviral nucleotide analogs, NSAIDs, methotrexate, and beta-lactams from blood into the tubular epithelium[4t][5t][6t][7t].

MATE1.logic: MATE1 (SLC47A1) is an apical multidrug and toxin extrusion transporter of proximal tubule cells. Driven by an oppositely directed proton gradient, it carries out electroneutral H+/organic-cation antiport, exporting cationic drugs and metabolites from the epithelium into the luminal filtrate.
MATE1.logic_cited: MATE1 (SLC47A1) is an apical multidrug and toxin extrusion transporter of proximal tubule cells[8][9]. Driven by an oppositely directed proton gradient, it carries out electroneutral H+/organic-cation antiport[10], exporting cationic drugs and metabolites from the epithelium into the luminal filtrate[8t].

COX2.logic: COX-2 (PTGS2) is an inducible prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase expressed in the macula densa, thick ascending limb, and medullary interstitial cells. There it generates prostaglandins that promote afferent arteriolar vasodilation, medullary blood flow, sodium excretion, and renin release.
COX2.logic_cited: COX-2 (PTGS2) is an inducible prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase[12] expressed in the macula densa[13], thick ascending limb, and medullary interstitial cells[13]. There it generates prostaglandins that promote afferent arteriolar vasodilation, medullary blood flow, sodium excretion[13], and renin release[13].

ACE.logic: ACE is a dipeptidyl carboxypeptidase that converts angiotensin I into the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II and degrades bradykinin. Angiotensin II preferentially constricts the efferent arteriole, sustaining glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure and filtration.
ACE.logic_cited: ACE is a dipeptidyl carboxypeptidase that converts angiotensin I into the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II[14] and degrades bradykinin[14t]. Angiotensin II preferentially constricts the efferent arteriole[40!], sustaining glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure and filtration[15t].

VEGFR2.logic: VEGFR2 (KDR) is the principal VEGF-A receptor tyrosine kinase on glomerular endothelial cells. Podocyte-derived VEGF-A signaling through VEGFR2 maintains endothelial fenestration, endothelial survival, and the integrity of the glomerular filtration barrier.
VEGFR2.logic_cited: VEGFR2 (KDR) is the principal VEGF-A receptor tyrosine kinase[18t] on glomerular endothelial cells[17]. Podocyte-derived VEGF-A signaling through VEGFR2 maintains endothelial fenestration[16t], endothelial survival, and the integrity of the glomerular filtration barrier[16t][19t].

pathway_rules: Renal transporter recognition and binding affinity are shared by many safe drugs and are necessary but not sufficient for injury; toxicity additionally requires intracellular accumulation to cytotoxic levels, luminal crystallization, or a measurable hemodynamic effect.

Anionic drugs taken up by basolateral OAT1 concentrate in proximal tubule cells; injury arises when high-affinity, actively secreted anions accumulate faster than apical efflux clears them, reaching levels that impair mitochondria and generate oxidative stress, whereas efficient efflux or low intrinsic cytotoxicity spares the tubule.

Cationic drugs depend on apical MATE1 export to leave the epithelium; injury occurs when efflux is saturated or impaired and cations accumulate intracellularly, whereas balanced uptake and efflux limit net accumulation.

Inhibition of renal COX-2 lowers prostaglandin-dependent afferent arteriolar vasodilation and GFR chiefly under volume depletion or pre-existing hypoperfusion; with normal perfusion the effect is usually functional and reversible.

Inhibition of the renin-angiotensin system reduces efferent arteriolar tone and intraglomerular pressure, producing a functional and typically reversible GFR decline that becomes injurious mainly when perfusion is already angiotensin II-dependent.

Direct tubular toxins and low-solubility drugs injure the kidney concentration-dependently: heavy-metal or platinum adducts drive oxidative tubular damage, and poorly soluble species precipitate as intratubular crystals causing obstruction; VEGFR2 inhibition separately disrupts glomerular endothelial integrity, causing proteinuria and thrombotic microangiopathy.

yes_features: Acyclic nucleotide phosphonate or phosphonamidate scaffold characteristic of antiviral nucleotide analogs: anionic, actively secreted, and concentrated in proximal tubule cells.
Polycationic aminocyclitol linked to aminosugars in an aminoglycoside architecture: reabsorbed by megalin-mediated endocytosis and retained in proximal tubule lysosomes.
Platinum or other heavy-metal coordination center: forms intracellular adducts and generates reactive oxygen species in tubular epithelium.
Poorly soluble sulfonamide or weakly acidic heterocycle that concentrates in the urinary pH range: predisposes to intratubular crystal precipitation and obstruction.
Arylalkanoic or enolic-acid nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory scaffold: inhibits renal COX and reduces prostaglandin-dependent perfusion.
Anti-angiogenic multi-kinase scaffold with VEGF-pathway activity (indolinone, aminoquinazoline, or pyridinyl-urea): disrupts glomerular endothelial integrity.
no_features: High plasma protein binding with a small free fraction: limits glomerular filtration and tubular delivery, minimizing renal parenchymal exposure.
Predominant hepatic or biliary clearance, with renal excretion of inactive metabolites rather than active parent drug.
Neutral, non-ionizable structure lacking anionic or cationic groups: poorly recognized by renal organic-anion and organic-cation transporters, limiting proximal tubule uptake.
High aqueous solubility maintained across the physiological urinary pH range (4.5-8.0): no propensity for intratubular crystallization.
Selective pharmacology without off-target COX, renin-angiotensin, or VEGFR activity: renal hemodynamics and the glomerular filtration barrier are preserved.
Rapid biotransformation to inactive, readily eliminated species: short tubular residence and low intracellular accumulation.

contradiction_flags.mla: Denton, K. M., et al. "Effects of Angiotensin II on Regional Afferent and Efferent Arteriole Dimensions and the Glomerular Pole." American Journal of Physiology. Regulatory, Integrative and Comparative Physiology, vol. 279, no. 2, 2000, pp. R629-38. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1152/ajpregu.2000.279.2.R629.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: Afferent diameter decreased more than efferent in the outer and mid cortex (P < 0.05) but by a similar extent in juxtamedullary nephrons (P = 0.58). Calculated efferent resistance increased more than afferent, especially in the outer cortex (127 vs. 24 units; 5 ng. kg(-1). min(-1) ANG II).
contradiction_flags.note: The diameter data do contradict 'preferentially constricts' the efferent vessel, but in the same span the resistance endpoint - the one the atom's next clause relies on for glomerular pressure - runs the clause's way, and the afferent predominance is regional. (Angiotensin II preferentially constricts the efferent arteriole.; Afferent diameter fell MORE than efferent in outer and mid cortex (similar in juxtamedullary nephrons), while calculated efferent resistance rose more than afferent (127 vs 24 units at 5 ng/kg/min).)
contradiction_flags.scope: anesthetized rabbits, intrarenal ANG II 0.1-5 ng/kg/min, vascular-casting diameters; afferent predominance holds in outer and mid cortex only (similar in juxtamedullary nephrons) and the calculated-resistance endpoint runs the other way

contradiction_flags.segment_text: Acyclic nucleotide phosphonate or phosphonamidate scaffold characteristic of antiviral nucleotide analogs: anionic, actively secreted, and concentrated in proximal tubule cells.
contradiction_flags.mla: Ray, Adrian S., et al. "Mechanism of Active Renal Tubular Efflux of Tenofovir." Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy, vol. 50, no. 10, 2006, pp. 3297-304. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.00251-06.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: TFV accumulated to fivefold lower levels in MRP4-overexpressing cells, and its accumulation could be increased by an MRP inhibitor.
contradiction_flags.note: On the fourth disputed question: the abstract reports the opposite of accumulation - 'TFV accumulated to fivefold lower levels in MRP4-overexpressing cells, and its accumulation could be increased by an MRP inhibitor', with those cells also 2.0- to 2.5-fold less susceptible to TFV cytotoxicity - and the systems are MRP4-overexpressing cell lines and MRP4-containing membrane vesicles, not proximal tubule cells. I therefore raise SCOPE_LIMITED to CONTRADICTED, since the atom's asserted intracellular concentration is the direction this paper's only accumulation data reverse; the active-secretion element alone survives and is scored in W033.

contradiction_flags.segment_text: High plasma protein binding with a small free fraction: limits glomerular filtration and tubular delivery,
contradiction_flags.mla: Masereeuw, Rosalinde, et al. "The Kidney and Uremic Toxin Removal: Glomerulus or Tubule?." Seminars in Nephrology, vol. 34, no. 2, 2014, pp. 191-208. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.semnephrol.2014.02.010.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: These uremic retention solutes, also known as uremic toxins, are a heterogeneous group of organic compounds, many are too large to be filtered (middle molecules) or are protein-bound. Tubular secretion shifts the binding and allows for active secretion of such solutes.
contradiction_flags.note: The same span supports the filtration half and denies the tubular-delivery half, so the flag is right about a real conflict but only for one named sub-clause and for a specific class of protein-bound solutes that are proximal-tubule transporter substrates. (High plasma protein binding with a small free fraction limits both glomerular filtration and tubular delivery.; Protein binding does keep these solutes from being filtered, but tubular secretion 'shifts the binding and allows for active secretion of such solutes', so bound solutes still reach the tubule.)
contradiction_flags.scope: Protein-bound uremic retention solutes handled by proximal-tubule OAT1/OAT3/OATP4C1 and ABC efflux pumps, as stated in a review; only the tubular-delivery half of the clause is touched.

contradiction_flags.segment_text: Neutral, non-ionizable structure lacking anionic or cationic groups: poorly recognized by renal organic-anion and organic-cation transporters,
contradiction_flags.mla: Betterton, Robert D., et al. "Organic Cation Transporter (OCT/OCTN) Expression at Brain Barrier Sites: Focus on CNS Drug Delivery." Handbook of Experimental Pharmacology, vol. 266, 2021, pp. 301-328. PubMed, https://doi.org/10.1007/164_2021_448.
contradiction_flags.contradicting_quote: Organic Cation Transporters (OCTs) and Novel Organic Cation Transporters (OCTNs) are two subfamilies of the solute carrier 22 (SLC22) family of proteins that have significant potential to mediate delivery of positively charged, zwitterionic, and uncharged therapeutics.
contradiction_flags.note: Uncharged compounds being plausible OCT/OCTN substrates is genuinely in tension with 'poorly recognized', since these isoforms are also renal, but the statement is a family-level capability claim made for CNS barrier sites and the abstract itself says functional expression there needs more analysis. Disclose the organ mismatch and the untouched OAT half. (Neutral, non-ionizable molecules lacking anionic or cationic groups are poorly recognized by renal organic-anion and organic-cation transporters.; OCTs and OCTNs, two SLC22 subfamilies, are described as having significant potential to mediate delivery of positively charged, zwitterionic AND uncharged therapeutics.)
contradiction_flags.scope: The organic-CATION side only (SLC22 OCT/OCTN substrate scope), stated as delivery 'potential' in a review of blood-brain and blood-CSF barrier transport; no renal proximal-tubule data and nothing about organic-anion transporters.
